metadata.name: tutorzy-meeting-room
metadata.description: A 1-on-1 teacher/student video meeting room with mic/camera controls (device picker), screen sharing, an Excalidraw-powered collaborative whiteboard (MIT licensed, free for commercial use), in-call chat with typing indicator, connection/audio-quality status, focus mode, keyboard shortcuts, local-only recording, and presence reporting used to confirm lesson attendance.
features: Peer-to-peer video/audio call via PeerJS with a device picker for multiple mics/cameras
Screen sharing shows your own share large, peer shrinks to a corner tile; combined peer+local camera box during sharing
Whiteboard is now powered by the real Excalidraw React SDK (MIT license, no cost, no watermark), loaded via ES modules from a CDN with no build step
Excalidraw brings its own full toolbar, color/style panel, undo/redo, zoom, and shape tools natively - none of that is custom-built anymore
Whiteboard state syncs between teacher and student by sending Excalidraw's element array over the existing WebRTC data channel
Teacher can lock the whiteboard so the student can only view, not draw
Save exports the current whiteboard as a PNG using Excalidraw's own export utility
Chat with a typing indicator, notification sound, and a clear-chat button
Focus mode hides everything but video and whiteboard; keyboard shortcuts: space to mute, R to record, W to toggle whiteboard
Manual reconnect button appears automatically when the connection is weak, plus a separate audio-quality indicator
Local-only recording composed from both video feeds via canvas, no screen-picker dialog
Emits presence ticks (join / heartbeat / leave) so attendance can be recorded server-side

Optional live captions (speech-to-text only, no translation) using the browser's own free built-in speech recognition - each side transcribes its own mic and sends the text to the peer over the existing data channel. NOT supported on iOS Safari/WebView (including inside the mobile app on iOS) - the captions button auto-hides there; works on desktop Chrome/Edge/Safari and Chrome on Android.

Mobile-responsive: a CSS media query (max-width: 480px) reflows the crowded top status bar, remote/local labels, local camera preview size, and toolbar for narrow viewports (e.g. inside a native app's WebView) without changing anything on wider/desktop viewports

properties.name: lessonId
properties.description: Unique lesson/room identifier shared by both participants.

properties.name: roomToken
properties.description: Secret per-lesson token mixed into the WebRTC room id.

properties.name: userRole
properties.description: Current user's role: teacher or student.

properties.name: teacherPhotoUrl
properties.description: Teacher's profile photo URL, shown as the big centered avatar while waiting for the teacher to join (falls back to an initial-letter circle if empty).

properties.name: studentPhotoUrl
properties.description: Student's profile photo URL, shown as the big centered avatar while waiting for the student to join (falls back to an initial-letter circle if empty).

properties.name: roomHeight
properties.description: CSS height of the meeting room.

properties.name: savedWhiteboardState
properties.description: JSON string of a previously saved whiteboard state, shape { elements: [...] }. NOTE: whiteboard states saved before the Excalidraw migration (Fabric.js format) are NOT compatible and will be silently ignored.

properties.name: lessonTitle
properties.description: Title shown in the top status bar.

properties.name: lessonEndIso
properties.description: ISO timestamp of when the lesson is scheduled to end. Powers the 5-minutes-left indicator.

properties.name: toolbarStyle
properties.description: glass or solid toolbar background (main call toolbar).

events.name: callStarted
events.description: Fires once both participants are connected.

events.name: callEnded
events.description: Fires after the user confirms they want to leave.

events.name: presence
events.description: Fires on join, then every 30 seconds, then on leave.

events.name: whiteboardChanged
events.description: Fires when whiteboard content changes (debounced ~1.2s). Payload is now { elements: [...Excalidraw elements] }, NOT the old Fabric.js format.

events.name: chatMessageSent
events.description: Fires when the local user sends a chat message.

events.name: lateJoinReminderRequested
events.description: Fires when the local user clicks 'Send reminder' on the late-join banner. Bind this to your own notification - the component itself does not send anything.

actions.label: Toggle Whiteboard
actions.description: Opens or closes the whiteboard modal.

actions.label: Load Whiteboard State
actions.description: Loads a previously saved whiteboard JSON state (Excalidraw format: { elements: [...] }).

args.name: state
args.description: JSON string of the saved whiteboard state.

specifications: Root element has no hardcoded width/height; height is controlled via the roomHeight property.
MAJOR CHANGE: the whiteboard engine switched from a hand-built Fabric.js implementation to the real Excalidraw SDK, loaded via ES module imports from esm.sh (no build step, no bundler).
Excalidraw is MIT licensed - completely free for commercial use, no watermark, no license key needed.
Excalidraw provides its own complete toolbar/color panel/undo-redo/zoom - none of that is custom code anymore.

REMOVED in this migration (not present in open-source Excalidraw, would need custom work to re-add): multi-page whiteboard support, multi-page PDF export, remote laser pointer / live cursor position, snap-to-grid, custom alignment guides, dark-mode canvas toggle, background pattern cycling.

This integration has NOT been verified in a live browser by the assistant - unlike the previous Fabric.js work, React-based rendering inside the iframe could not be tested through this text-based tool. Live testing by the user is required after publishing.
Whiteboard sync sends Excalidraw's full element array over the P2P data channel on every change (debounced ~180ms) - works the same way the old 'full sync' did, just with a different payload shape.

Mobile-only CSS overrides live inside a single @media (max-width: 480px) block appended at the very end of the <style> tag. All rules above that block are the original desktop styles and are untouched by this change - narrow viewports (like the mobile app's WebView) get a reflowed status bar, smaller local camera preview, and a more compact toolbar; anything wider than 480px renders exactly as before.
